findings.title: include_website_name is not a predicate method, so the attribute is always serialized
findings.body: The method is named `include_website_name` (without a trailing `?`), but ActiveModel::Serializers only calls `include_<attr>?` predicate methods to decide whether to include an attribute. Because no `include_website_name?` method exists, the serializer falls back to always including `website_name`. This means `website_name` is serialized for every user regardless of whether `website` is present, and — more importantly — it bypasses the `untrusted_attributes` guard declared on line 43. For a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous user, `restrict_user_fields?` should suppress `website` (and its derived `website_name`), but since the predicate is never consulted, the derived display name (which embeds the host and path of the user's website) leaks to anonymous viewers even when the raw `website` attribute is correctly hidden. The method should be renamed to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Subdomain comparison logic is wrong for multi-label domains and misclassifies sibling subdomains
findings.body: The branch `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` compares only the *last two labels* (`split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`) of each host. For hosts with more than three labels this is incorrect: e.g. website_host `a.b.example.com` (4 labels) vs discourse_host `c.d.example.com` (4 labels) — `split('.')[1..-1]` yields `b.example.com` vs `d.example.com`, which differ, so it returns just the host (acceptable), but website_host `x.forum.example.com` vs discourse_host `y.forum.example.com` yields `forum.example.com` == `forum.example.com`, so it wrongly treats a *sibling* subdomain as the same site and appends the path. Conversely, the intended same-registrable-domain check should compare the registrable domain (last two labels for common TLDs), not `split('.')[1..-1]`. The logic also fails for two-label discourse hosts (e.g. `example.com` vs `www.example.com` falls into the `else` branch, which only handles the parent-domain case via `ends_with?`, missing the `www.` child case). The consequence is incorrect display of full paths for unrelated sibling subdomains and missed path display for legitimate same-site subdomains.

findings.title: URI parsing is performed multiple times and `rescue nil` swallows all StandardError
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed three separate times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149) instead of once, which is wasteful and can produce inconsistent results if `website` changes between calls (it cannot here, but the repetition is fragile). More importantly, `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` uses a bare `rescue` modifier that catches all `StandardError` subclasses, not just `URI::InvalidURIError`. A `website` value that raises an unexpected error (e.g. a `NoMethodError` from a misbehaving `to_s`, or an `ArgumentError` from deeply malformed input) would be silently swallowed and treated as "no host", causing `website_name` to return nil. The rescue should be scoped to `URI::InvalidURIError` (and ideally `URI::BadURIError`), and the URI should be parsed once into a local variable.

findings.title: Path is appended without preserving query string or fragment, and root path yields a trailing host with no separator semantics
findings.body: When the website host matches the instance host, the code returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. This drops the query string and fragment entirely (e.g. `http://example.com/page?x=1` displays as `example.com/page`), and for a bare root URL like `http://example.com` the path is `""` (or `/`), producing `example.com` or `example.com/` — the latter with a dangling slash. The display name is meant to show the complete URL path per the PR title, so query/fragment omission is a functional gap; at minimum the behavior for root paths should be normalized (no trailing slash).

findings.title: Untrusted-attributes test does not include website_name, so the privacy leak is not covered
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list on line 11 is `%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}` — it does not include `website_name`, even though `website_name` was added to `untrusted_attributes` in the serializer (line 43 of user_serializer.rb). Because the `include_website_name` predicate is broken (missing `?`), `website_name` is always serialized; the test asserting that untrusted attributes are absent for a TL0 user seen anonymously would not catch this leak because `website_name` is not in the list. The test should add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and also assert that it is absent when `website` is blank for trusted viewers.

findings.title: No test covers the sibling-subdomain or www-child cases that the comparison logic mishandles
findings.body: The new specs only cover three cases: different domain (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), exact match (`example.com`), and parent-domain (`forums.example.com` with website `example.com`). There is no test for sibling subdomains of equal label count (e.g. website `blog.example.com` on instance `forums.example.com`, which the current `split('.')[1..-1]` logic would wrongly treat as same-site for three-label hosts only if the middle labels match — actually it compares `example.com` == `example.com` and would append the path incorrectly), nor for the `www.` child case (`www.example.com` website on `example.com` instance, which falls into the `else` branch and fails the `ends_with?` check, returning only the host). These edge cases are exactly where the comparison logic is fragile, so tests should pin down the intended behavior.
